cards.explanation: The answer is length of days and peace. The speaker says his commandments "…will add length to your days, years and peace to your life." (Proverbs 3:2) Days AND peace in the same deal, friends. That's a better package than anything I ever found in a junk drawer.

The answer is on the tablet of his heart. The speaker says to "…write them on the tablet of your heart." (Proverbs 3:3) So this isn't something you stick on the fridge, friends. It goes deep, like a stamp pressed all the way into the dough.
The answer is False. The speaker says you will find "…favor and high regard in the sight of God and man." (Proverbs 3:4) Both are in there, friends. He doesn't leave people out of the deal.

The answer is acknowledge. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him…" (Proverbs 3:6) All your ways, friends, not just the Sunday ones. I'd say that covers the Monday morning ones too, and I'm looking at myself with that one.

The answer is False. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight." (Proverbs 3:6) He's the one who makes the paths straight, friends. That's a lot less work for the son.

The answer is fear the LORD and turn from evil. Instead of being wise in his own eyes, the son is told to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." (Proverbs 3:7) That's the swap, friends: quit acting like you've got it all figured out and look up instead. I've read my own recipe, said "I know better," and had the dough set me straight.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." and verse 8 follows with, "This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones." (Proverbs 3:7-8) Healing and refreshment come right after, friends. My old bones are listening.

The answer is that they will be filled with plenty. The speaker says, "…then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine." (Proverbs 3:10) Full barns, overflowing vats, friends. I'd call that a very full pantry.

The answer is that the LORD disciplines the one He loves. The speaker says, "…for the LORD disciplines the one He loves…" (Proverbs 3:12) That's the reason he gives, friends. The discipline comes with love, and that's worth remembering when it stings.

The answer is True. The verse says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, "…as does a father the son in whom he delights." (Proverbs 3:12) A father who delights in his son and still disciplines him, friends. I know a thing or two about that picture.

The answer is better. The speaker says wisdom "…is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold." (Proverbs 3:14) Then he says she's "…more precious than rubies…" (Proverbs 3:15) Silver, gold and rubies all come in second, friends.
The answer is long life. The verse says, "Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor." (Proverbs 3:16) Wisdom shows up with both hands full, friends.
The answer is True. The verse says, "All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful." (Proverbs 3:17) Pleasant AND peaceful, friends, and the word is ALL both times. That's a good road.

The answer is wisdom. The verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" (Proverbs 3:19) The speaker has just been praising wisdom, friends, and here the LORD founded the earth by it. The same verse says He "…established the heavens by understanding."
The answer is False. The verse says, "By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open…" (Proverbs 3:20) Not sealed shut, friends. Then the clouds dripped with dew.
